memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'The land must not be sold permanently, because the land is mine and you
reside in my land as foreigners and strangers'" - Lev 25:23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the truth at the heart of the whole Jubilee system. The land could
not be permanently sold because it never truly belonged to the people in
the first place. It was God's. They were tenants, residents, guests on land
that had only one true owner.

That single conviction reshaped everything — how they farmed, traded,
treated the poor, and held their possessions. You handle differently what
you know is only lent to you.

Dear friend, we desperately need this perspective. We speak of "my house,
my money, my career, my time," and slowly we come to believe we are owners
rather than stewards. But the psalmist says the earth is the LORD's, and
everything in it (Ps 24:1). We came into the world with nothing, and we
will take nothing out of it (1 Tim 6:7).

Everything you have is on loan. Your abilities, your possessions, even your
years — all entrusted, none owned outright.

This is humbling, but it is also freeing. If you are a steward and not an
owner, then the pressure of ultimate responsibility is not yours. You are
managing what belongs to a good and generous Master.

Jesus told parables of stewards who would give an account of what their
master entrusted to them (Matt 25:14-30). Hold everything with an open
hand today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I live as an owner or as a steward of what God has entrusted?
2. What am I gripping too tightly as though it were ultimately mine?
3. How would seeing myself as a tenant change how I use my resources?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, everything I have is Yours, lent to me for a while. Loosen my grip,
make me a faithful steward, and free me from the burden of imagined
ownership. Amen.
